transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2026-09-01 15:00 PT
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Jenna (Evergreen Head of InfoSec), Mark (CTO), Alex (SRE), Priya (Product)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
Redwood team walked through high-level security posture. Customer asked about SOC2, ISO, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration and data retention especially for PHI. Redwood committed to sending compliance artifacts and follow-up deep-dive for dedicated/private deployment.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood Inference, and with me is Carlos, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:08] Jenna (Evergreen): Hi, thanks. Doing well. We set aside 45 minutes to go through security posture — high level today and then get into specifics.
[00:00:15] Carlos (Redwood): Great. We'll keep it focused. Quick agenda: compliance evidence (SOC2/ISO), auth (SSO/SAML, SCIM), RBAC, logging/audit & retention, encryption/KMS, and then deployment modes — hosted vs dedicated vs private — and recommended next steps.
[00:00:30] Mark (Evergreen): Sounds good. Our main driver is PHI handling for a couple of features, so we need to figure out whether Hosted is viable or if we need Dedicated or Private.
[00:00:37] Priya (Evergreen): And timelines — we have a pilot starting in Q4, want to know what runway is for security reviews.
[00:00:45] Carlos (Redwood): Understood. Starting with compliance: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, and we're progressing on ISO 27001 — we can share the certs and the control mapping. I'll drop the SOC2 report and the control matrix after the call.
[00:00:58] Jenna (Evergreen): Is the SOC2 scoped to both Hosted and Dedicated? We need to confirm coverage for dedicated / private deployments and whether any controls change if we go on-prem.
[00:01:06] Maya (Redwood): Good question. SOC2 covers our Hosted control plane and hosted infra; Dedicated has a different scoping note — we provide a framework and controls but some operational controls fall on the customer depending on configuration. For Private/on-prem, customers operate the infra so they'd handle physical and some ops controls; we provide a compliance package and runbooks. We'll annotate the SOC2 for these differences.
[00:01:29] Alex (Evergreen): For PHI, do you support a Business Associate Agreement?
[00:01:33] Maya (Redwood): Yes, we have a BAA option for enterprise customers; legal team can share a template.
[00:01:38] Jenna (Evergreen): Good. Next, SSO. We use Okta and require SAML 2.0 for authentication and SCIM for provisioning.
[00:01:46] Carlos (Redwood): We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning. For Hosted, SSO is supported for the Console and API access tokens can be tied to SSO sessions via short-lived tokens and RBAC. I should note the auto-generated token lifetimes can be tuned — we have both OIDC and SAML flows.
[00:02:04] Mark (Evergreen): When you say API tokens tied to SSO, do you do exchange or just manual token issuance? We prefer token exchange with short TTLs and automated rotation.
[00:02:12] Carlos (Redwood): Right now we support automated provisioning and short-lived tokens through an OIDC token exchange flow; for Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS or key broker for rotation. There's a little nuance — some older systems require static tokens; we discourage that for PHI.
[00:02:28] Jenna (Evergreen): SCIM for provisioning users and groups is a hard requirement. Can you support group sync and SCIM SCHEMAS we have?
[00:02:35] Carlos (Redwood): Yes, SCIM group sync is supported. We have a mapping template for group->RBAC role mapping; I'll share the sample metadata XML and SCIM endpoint docs. FYI sometimes the auto-parse of attributes in our doc generator misses custom attributes — but we'll provide a canonical example.
[00:02:52] Priya (Evergreen): Great. On RBAC: we want least privilege, ability to restrict model deployment to specific teams, and separation of duties between infra ops and product folks.
[00:03:03] Carlos (Redwood): Our RBAC supports role-based policies with per-route and per-model scopes. You can create custom roles, enforce MFA, and audit role changes. For Dedicated/Private, RBAC can be hooked to your LDAP/SSO via SCIM claims.
[00:03:18] Alex (Evergreen): How are admin actions logged? We need immutable logs for audit and eDiscovery.
[00:03:23] Maya (Redwood): We export audit logs to a customer-managed S3 or to a SIEM (Splunk, Datadog, Sumo). Logs include user id, action, timestamp, request metadata. For Hosted we retain logs by default 90 days but can do longer retention as an enterprise add-on.
[00:03:40] Jenna (Evergreen): 90 days might not meet our regulatory retention — for PHI we might need 7 years for certain artifacts. Can you do long-term export?
[00:03:48] Carlos (Redwood): Yes — we can set up streaming of logs to your S3 bucket for indefinite retention. We also support object immutability/lifecycle policies on your side. We'll include guidance for log redaction and PII masking options in transit.
[00:04:05] Mark (Evergreen): On the topic of audit logs, do you provide tamper-evident hashes or chain-of-custody metadata?
[00:04:12] Carlos (Redwood): We provide monotonically-incrementing event ids and signed metadata for key events; tamper-proofing is generally implemented by customers on their S3 buckets (WORM / object lock). We can additionally provide a signed manifest on request.
[00:04:27] Priya (Evergreen): Encryption — at rest and in transit — what's the model and can we use our own KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / HSM)?
[00:04:35] Maya (Redwood): All data in transit is TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3. At rest we encrypt using AES-256. For Hosted we use provider-managed keys by default but support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS and equivalent in other clouds for Dedicated; for Private/on-prem we integrate with on-prem HSMs and your KMS. We'll provide KMS integration docs and a list of supported algorithms.
[00:04:56] Alex (Evergreen): If we use customer-managed keys, do you have access to the plaintext or to the key material?
[00:05:02] Carlos (Redwood): With CMKs configured via KMS, key material remains in your KMS; Redwood requests decrypt operations via KMS APIs as-needed. For Dedicated with VPC endpoints we can restrict network egress so requests to KMS stay in your VPC — we can architect it to minimize Redwood access.
[00:05:19] Jenna (Evergreen): Are model weights considered sensitive? We sometimes use fine-tuned models trained on patient data. Where are those stored and encrypted?
[00:05:27] Carlos (Redwood): We treat model artifacts as customer-owned when you upload them to Dedicated or Private. For Hosted we store them encrypted in tenant-isolated buckets; for fine-tuned weights you can choose to store them in your own S3 and reference them. We'll call out that if you send training data to us for fine-tuning on Hosted, you should consider Dedicated/Private.
[00:05:46] Priya (Evergreen): Any native DLP or data masking on prompts/outputs?
[00:05:51] Carlos (Redwood): We have a rules engine for redaction and pre-send filters; for PHI workflows we recommend customer-side preprocessing and prefix/KV caching rules to avoid storing raw PHI. We also offer post-response redaction hooks.
[00:06:07] Mark (Evergreen): Let's talk about data retention of prompts and logs — what are defaults and options? We need configurable retention per route/model.
[00:06:15] Maya (Redwood): Defaults: ephemeral request logs for 30 days, audit logs 90 days. We can configure per-customer, per-route retention and export to customer S3 for long-term. For Dedicated/Private, you control retention. We'll provide a retention config spec.
[00:06:31] Jenna (Evergreen): For eDiscovery you mentioned metadata — can you search logs for user ids, request ids, and export bundles?
[00:06:38] Carlos (Redwood): Yes — our log export includes request ids and trace ids. We can create export bundles and support legal hold workflows if needed.
[00:06:46] Priya (Evergreen): A couple of nitty gritty network questions: do you support VPC peering, PrivateLink, or only public endpoints?
[00:06:54] Carlos (Redwood): We support PrivateLink and VPC peering for Dedicated and Private, plus customer-managed NAT/Egress controls. For Hosted we have regional endpoints and IP allowlisting. We'll include a network diagram in the follow-up.
[00:07:06] Alex (Evergreen): How are secrets handled in CI/CD? We need to rotate keys used by our pipelines.
[00:07:12] Carlos (Redwood): We integrate with secrets managers; tokens can be short-lived and rotated via the OIDC exchange. For Dedicated, tokens can be issued by your IDP and we can consume them via mutual TLS or SPIFFE if needed.
[00:07:25] Jenna (Evergreen): Any penetration test or vulnerability scanning cadence you can share?
[00:07:30] Maya (Redwood): We run quarterly vulnerability scanning and annual external pen-tests. We can share an executive summary of findings and remediation timelines.
[00:07:38] Mark (Evergreen): SLA and incident response — how do you surface security incidents and what's the RTO/RPO for data recovery?
[00:07:45] Carlos (Redwood): We have incident response playbooks; for enterprise customers there's a dedicated channel and an SLA-backed incident response window. RTO/RPO vary by deployment — Hosted has cross-region backups with typical RTO under 4 hours for critical control plane, Dedicated options can meet stricter RTOs depending on reserved capacity.
[00:08:04] Priya (Evergreen): For the pilot, if we start with Hosted and then move to Dedicated, how disruptive is migration?
[00:08:11] Carlos (Redwood): We try to make it seamless: model versioning and API semantics are consistent. Migration complexity is mostly around model artifact location and KMS key changes. We'll provide a migration checklist.
[00:08:23] Jenna (Evergreen): One more question: do you maintain access logs down to token-level cost attribution? We want to correlate usage to business units for chargeback.
[00:08:31] Maya (Redwood): Yes, cost attribution and token-level breakdown is available via Console; we can provide per-route and per-API-key usage exports.
[00:08:39] Mark (Evergreen): Any known limitations with our stack? We're AWS and use EKS, Okta, and HashiCorp Vault.
[00:08:46] Carlos (Redwood): All three are common. For Vault we can integrate via transit secrets engine for encryption operations; for EKS we recommend Dedicated with VPC integration. We'll include a sample infra diagram showing Vault + KMS + Redwood endpoints.
[00:09:00] Priya (Evergreen): Awesome. For evidence, can you send SOC2, ISO summary, pen test summary, and the architecture doc?
[00:09:08] Maya (Redwood): Absolutely. I'll package SOC2 Type II redacted report, ISO summary, and the pen test exec summary. Carlos will draft the Dedicated/VPC architecture and KMS patterns.
[00:09:19] Jenna (Evergreen): We'll also send our retention requirements and the Okta metadata.
[00:09:24] Maya (Redwood): Great — sounds like next steps are clear.
[00:09:28] Mark (Evergreen): Quick logistics — can we schedule the dedicated deep-dive for next week?
[00:09:33] Carlos (Redwood): I'm available Tue/Thu morning PST. I'll send a calendar invite.
[00:09:38] Priya (Evergreen): Prefer Thursday.
[00:09:40] Maya (Redwood): Noted.
[00:09:42] Alex (Evergreen): One small thing — in your docs, make sure 'KV cache' and inferencing terms are clarified; we had an earlier call where terminology was slightly different and confused the infra team.
[00:09:51] Carlos (Redwood): Good call-out; I'll annotate the glossary and include the runtime terms (KV cache vs prefix cache, batching behavior).
[00:09:59] Maya (Redwood): Ok I'll recap. Action items and timeline on the follow-up email. Thanks everyone.
[00:10:06] Jenna (Evergreen): Thanks all.
[00:10:09] Mark (Evergreen): Thanks.
[00:10:12] Priya (Evergreen): Bye.
